body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-HIMS:q4-2026-adj-ebitda-80m-plus`
- **Method:** management-tone-vs-delivery · **P(ours)** 0.40 · **P(base)** 0.50 · resolve by 2027-03-10
- **Evidence:** 8-K 9-Nov-2026 (Q3 2026): revenue +49% YoY (second straight quarter of acceleration). Guidance: Q4 revenue $875–895M, adjusted EBITDA $70–90M (8–10% margin); FY2026 revenue tightened to $3.13–3.15B and adjusted EBITDA reduced to $257–277M. CFO Yemi Okupe: 'deliberate strategic decisions to position… for durable, multi-year growth' (i.e., investment over margin).
- **Why our number differs from base:** A company that just cut its EBITDA guide while framing it as 'deliberate investment' tends to keep spending; the 20M-wide range invites a sub-midpoint print. Lean below coin-flip.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Coin-flip for landing at/above a guidance midpoint (~50%).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if HIMS's reported Q4 2026 adjusted EBITDA (Q4 earnings release) ≥ $80.0M.
- **Resolution source:** Hims & Hers Q4 2026 earnings 8-K (SEC EDGAR, CIK 1773751)
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1773751/000177375126000242/hims-20260930x8xkearningsr.htm

body:
- **FY25 new leases:** 141 new store leases with average ~10-year terms and **$258.0M of minimum payments** → $1.83M per lease → **~$183k a year minimum rent ≈ $19.3/sq ft** at 9,500 sq ft [EST].
- **Feb–Mar 2026:** 27 leases, $48.0M → $178k a year. That is flat, with no rent inflation visible.
- **Variable lease cost** (CAM, taxes, %-rent) is $103.4M, 23% of the $449.9M net lease cost. Gross occupancy is ~$24–26/sq ft [EST].
- **Cash vs expense:** cash lease payments of $316.9M < straight-line operating lease cost of $346.5M, because of free-rent periods and growth.
- **Remaining lease term is 7.0 years.** Leases "typically have ten-year terms with additional five-year renewal options, and many provide us with the option to terminate early" `[10K25 Item 2]`. That is cheap optionality, and a US analogue of the Ind AS 116 lock-in question.

body:
| Rule | Part A (pre-T) | Part B (2020 → 2025) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1a fake-cash signal | 1/43 traps, 0 winners | not tested | **KEEP hard.** Add the mechanical test: interest income / avg cash vs FD rate; big cash + big debt |
| H1b economics implausible for the business | 3 traps, 0 winners (judgment); blind proxy fires on 5/28 winners | not tested | **KEEP hard, but ADJUST:** fires only after a written peer + bottom-up unit-economics comparison (revenue per outlet × outlets etc.); a ratio threshold alone is not the rule |
| H1c profits not verifiable by outsiders | 2 traps, 0 winners | not tested | **KEEP hard**; make "OPM < 2% on pass-through revenue" and "profit in a segment/partner we can't audit" explicit |
| H2 auditor exit over disagreement | 0/41 before T: always came after the peak | R3 (any resignation): no 5y lift, to-date 13% vs 3% (p 0.03, n 4) | **KEEP as a non-overridable EXIT / no-new-buy trigger** (it fires mid-collapse); note it almost never helps at entry |
| H2b broad (restatement, regulator-found misstatement, delayed results, any auditor exit within 5y) | +3 traps (Yes Bank, SMCI and Celsius peaks), cost 1 winner (SMCI 2023) | R3 ≈ this; flagged winners incl. CG Power 31x | **ADD as GRADED** (strong graded flag; RBI divergence for banks should be near-hard) |
| H3 rating not cooperating | 0 fires | not tested | **KEEP** (cheap, detector exists); unproven |
| H4 SME/pump pattern | only its own source cases | not tested | **KEEP**; extend to pre-revenue SPAC/IPO hype (Nikola) |
| H5 RPT cash leakage | 1 trap pre-T (Gitanjali); usually surfaces after T | not tested | **KEEP hard** |
| G1 pledge > 25% | 8/20 traps vs 2/13 winners (best graded flag) | x3 69% vs 51%; >50% & mcap ≥ 400 cr: loss 10% vs 1.4% (p 0.05) | **KEEP graded**; raise attention level at >50% or rising; never hard (Apollo, Suzlon-2020) |
| G3 dilution | 1 trap, 3 winners | not tested | **KEEP graded** (judge price × purpose × buyer) |
| G4 P/E > 50 | 7/9 busts, 4 winners | not tested | **MOVE to stage 5** (valuation temperature, P/E vs own median) — not a stage-2 filter |
| F1 / F1b CFO/PAT | traps 6/20 vs winners 8/24; frauds pass it | R1: no loss lift, x3 60% vs 52% | **DROP as a filter; keep as a question** ("what is the working capital made of?") |
| G2 debt + negative CFO | 2 traps vs 4 winners | R4: 0 losers in 27, x3 70% | **DROP as a filter; ADJUST** to a solvency rule (see below) |
| G5 negative FCF | 9 traps vs 15 winners | not tested separately | **DROP as a flag** (description only) |
| G6 debtor days | 3 vs 3 | not tested | **KEEP graded only with counterparty** (sovereign vs related/unknown, per L12) |
| F2 other income > 30% PBT | 6 vs 6 (fires on exchanges, PSU cash piles) | R5: loss 2.7% vs 0.7% (p 0.15), x3 61% vs 48% | **KEEP as a question** (it's where the H1a cash-yield test starts), not a flag |
title: hard_filters_test › VERDICT (both parts) and proposed revision

body:
1. **Three branches:** Aluva/Kochi (mature), a 2025–26 metro opening (Mumbai/Bengaluru), a semi-urban TN branch.
   Count counters, gold-loan desk queue, RMs; photograph the SA/TD rate boards and the gold-loan rate card; ask LTV.
2. **Gold-loan price check** (quarterly, fixed basket): FBL vs SBI/Canara/IOB vs Muthoot/Manappuram at 3 PIN codes.
3. **Gold auction notices** in Kerala newspapers (public, dated): count per quarter as a leading stress series.
4. **NRI channel:** two Gulf exchange houses and NRI depositors — FCNR leverage terms (deposit vs loan rate), stickiness after maturity.
5. **RBI data:** BSR state-wise deposits/credit (Kerala share); RBI monthly card statistics (verify 3.13%/1.90%); NPCI
   UPI bank performance; RBI Ombudsman annual complaints by bank.
6. **Fintech partners:** list them (app T&Cs, co-brand card pages), check app status and any RBI direction.
7. **Labour:** AIBEA/AIBOC notices on the 13th bipartite settlement; job-portal reviews for RM targets/attrition.
8. **Subsidiaries:** Fedbank Financial quarterly results (listed); FedServ MCA filings (outsourced ops cost).
9. **Bureau:** CRIF/TransUnion reports for gold, MFI, CV delinquency by lender type.
Each observation must change a number in §3.3–3.7 (rule of the protocol).
